key_facts: This document applies to all teams and officials at the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix on 13-15 March 2026.
The Race Director sets out rules for safe and orderly conduct during practice sessions, Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, Sprint, and Race.
Drivers must not exceed maximum times between Safety Car lines during qualifying and reconnaissance laps, or they may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly.
Drivers caught by faster cars must allow them past at the first available opportunity when blue light panels are shown at 1.2 seconds gap.
Specific procedures are set for pit lane access, starting procedures, practice starts, grid procedures, and track limits.
plain_explanation:
This document gives instructions for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix to make sure the race and qualifying sessions run safely and fairly.

The Race Director explains when drivers go too slowly. Any driver who takes longer than the maximum time between the Second Safety Car Line and the First Safety Car Line during Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, or reconnaissance laps may be judged to be going unnecessarily slowly. This can happen on any lap, including laps when a driver comes into or leaves the pit lane. Teams will be told what the maximum time is after practice.

During the Sprint and Race, the rules require drivers who are caught by a faster car to let that car pass as soon as possible. If a faster car gets within 1.2 seconds of a slower car, blue light panels will be shown as a signal. The driver of the slower car must then let the faster driver through at the first chance.

The document sets out rules for pit lane safety. Team staff can only be in the pit lane just before they need to work on a car, and must leave as soon as the work is finished. After the race ends and all cars have entered the Parc Fermé area (a controlled parking area where cars stay), the Race Director will send a message saying pit lane access rules no longer apply.

Practice starts are only allowed on the grid or pit exit road during specific times. Drivers cannot do practice starts during Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, or during the actual Sprint or Race. When reconnaissance laps happen before the Sprint or Race, drivers can do practice starts by stopping at a white line at pit exit, but they must not cross another white line and must stay in the correct part of the pit exit road.

The document explains pit entry and pit exit procedures. Drivers must follow marked white lines. At pit exit, drivers can only use the line painted on the track at pit exit and the line continuing after the Second Safety Car line.

Starting procedures require grid light panels to flash blue for 5 seconds before the lights go out for the start. After any standing start or restart, Driver Adjustable Bodywork in straight mode will be enabled after Turn 1.

Other rules cover when sessions can be stopped, how drivers must be weighed after qualifying, where cars can be removed from the grid, and where fire extinguishers and emergency equipment are located on the circuit. The document also notes small changes to the circuit, including a lower kerb at Turn 3 and moved tyre barriers.
